newsitem.title: CHINA: Fewer China farmers join exodus to cities.
newsitem.headline: Fewer China farmers join exodus to cities.

text.p: Fewer Chinese farmers are leaving their homes in search of high-paying jobs in cities, due in part to the introduction of curbs on migrant workers by some local authorities, an official said on Tuesday.

About three to four percent of China's rural population of 900 million joined the rush to work in cities last year compared with six to seven percent a year earlier, Xian Zude, deputy director of the State Statistical Bureau's agricultural department, told a news conference.
Xian gave no figure for the total number of farmers working in cities, but local newspapers have put the "floating population" at between 70-100 million. He gave no further details.
Some cities have introduced curbs to limit the number of migrant workers, blaming the immigrants for rising crime and worsening pollution.
Many migrant workers have also found it tougher to find jobs in cities due to competition from workers laid off by lumbering state enterprises.
